heroHeadline: 6 Days to Kickoff — Iran Players Submit Passports to US Embassy in Ankara; Squad Departs Antalya June 6; France Beaten by Ivory Coast in Historic First; Netherlands Fall to Algeria
heroSubtitle: Iran's World Cup visa crisis reached a critical inflection point on June 5 when football federation president Mehdi Taj announced that players have formally submitted their passports to the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey for processing — the first direct engagement with US consular procedures in the entire saga, 6 days before their June 15 Group G opener vs New Zealand at SoFi Stadium. Taj expressed confidence that visas would be issued 'soon' while issuing the clearest ultimatum yet: if applications are denied or receive no response before June 15, Iran's federation will 'reconsider participation.' The squad departs Antalya on June 6 — a day earlier than originally announced — following the June 3 issuance of Mexican visas through Turkish-Mexican embassy coordination. Iran conducted their final closed-door warm-up against Mali in Antalya on June 4 before heading to their Tijuana base camp. In pre-tournament friendly action, Ivory Coast made history on June 4 by beating France 1-2 in Nantes — the first time in international football history that Côte d'Ivoire have defeated France; Rayan Cherki had given Les Bleus the lead before Guela Doue and Amad Diallo completed the comeback. The Netherlands suffered a 0-1 defeat to Algeria at De Kuip on June 3, with Anis Hadj Moussa's 85th-minute curler proving the only goal. Spain drew 1-1 with Iraq in La Coruña on June 4 — Merchas Doski's long-range equalizer the first Iraq goal against Spain. Switzerland's Breel Embolo resolved his US visa issue on June 4 after a 2-day hold. Japan switched training facilities in Monterrey from the Tigres to the Rayados complex due to poor pitch conditions. FIFA revealed all players in the squad will stand in a circle around the centre circle during national anthems. The tournament opens in 6 days at Estadio Azteca: Mexico vs South Africa, June 11.
